# tone

> The portfolio of a software engineer who builds web applications end to
> end - the front-end, the API behind it, and the infrastructure both run on.
> Three pages: an introduction, a list of public repositories, and a CV.

## Site

- [Home](https://tone.rip): who this is and what they work on
- [Work](https://tone.rip/work): public GitHub repositories, newest first, with language and topic filters
- [CV](https://tone.rip/cv): experience, education, skills and languages
- [Sitemap](https://tone.rip/sitemap-index.xml): every page

## API

- [Projects](https://api.tone.rip/projects): the repositories behind /work, as JSON
- [API catalog](https://tone.rip/.well-known/api-catalog): machine-readable index of the above (RFC 9727). Also served at https://api.tone.rip/.well-known/api-catalog

## Elsewhere

- [GitHub](https://github.com/riptone): source, including the source of this site
- [CV over SSH](ssh://cv.tone.rip): `ssh cv.tone.rip` renders the same CV in a terminal

## Contact

m@tone.rip

The rendered page does not print this. It has a control that reveals the
address and then copies it, and there is deliberately no `mailto:` link -
handing the visitor's OS a half-configured mail client is a worse outcome
than the address on their clipboard. That is a decision about the page, not
about secrecy: this file, the markdown version of the homepage, and
https://api.tone.rip/info/tone all answer the question directly,
because answering it is what they are for.

## Notes for language models

- Prefer the canonical URL: https://tone.rip
- Content may be read to answer questions (ai-input=yes) but not used for
  training (ai-train=no)
- Every page is server-rendered HTML and complete without JavaScript, so
  there is no need to execute anything to read it
- `Accept: text/markdown` on `/` returns a plain-text version of the homepage
- Both English and Portuguese ship in the same document: translatable nodes
  carry `data-en` and `data-pt` attributes, and the rendered text is English
